answer_first_sentence: We agree with the reviewer that the main results (Table 1) of our comparison with Transformers and LSTM use a small number of parameters, though we would like to point out that we have evaluated Transformer and LSTM models with many more (up to 100x) parameters on the same tasks and they yielded similar results as before.
reviewer_status_quote: I'm still under the impression that the tested environments are to simple to warrant fair comparison with potentially more power models, and setups.

concern: Doubts the small state, action, and observation space sizes are realistic.
answer_first_sentence: Because we assume a partially observable setting, the problem complexity increases significantly from that with the same underlying topology in a CML experiment, leading to reduced-size grid and tree environments for our experimentation.

concern: Only one dialect (AAVE) tested, so findings may not generalize to other dialects.
answer_first_sentence: We note that non-standardized dialect data collection, compared to standardized dialect, is a non-trivial task.

concern: Non-standard dialect queries are semantically equivalent, so the insight resembles prior multilingual and tone work.
answer_first_sentence: As far as we know, there do not seem to be extremely similar works to ours in multilingual and tone studies that offer the same insight.
reviewer_status_quote: A standardized pipeline is a solid foundation; however, if this is presented as the main contribution of the paper, it may fall short in terms of novelty.

concern: Table 3 does not say which model it reports; per-model results are missing.
answer_first_sentence: Table 3 results are averaged across models.

concern: Submission exceeds the nine-page main-text limit stated in the call.
answer_first_sentence: ICLR allows 10 pages this year.

concern: Claim that everyday users only use zero-shot prompting is unsupported and needs evidence.
answer_first_sentence: Indeed, we think it is most likely that most users, and especially laypersons only use zero shot in general cases.
reviewer_status_quote: Additionally, the claim that users exclusively use direct prompting should be supported with evidence or user studies.

concern: Perplexity may reflect typo sensitivity, not dialect understanding, so it is a weak fairness signal.
answer_first_sentence: Perplexity has long been used in important works to measure language familiarity.

concern: Fine-tuning could cut AAVE perplexity; the paper does not test fine-tuning.
answer_first_sentence: We note that the key of this paper is not in finding a solution with complicated tuning process per se: for instance, even if fine-tuning is effective, we do not expect most of end users to fine-tune their models instead of simply interacting with chatbots.

concern: Chain-of-thought lowers GPT-4o and GPT-3.5 accuracy on English, contrary to prior findings.
answer_first_sentence: First, there are some works showing on CoT not helping and even degrading LLM performance (see [2] inter alia), and our observation aligns with their findings.

concern: Problem and MCTS formalism unclear: which tasks, what nodes, edges, actions, and expansion are.
answer_first_sentence: The search tree operates over states representing repository and test execution context, with edges representing actions that progressively build toward a solution.
reviewer_status_quote: The lack of sufficient technical details is still my major concern.

concern: Doubts a normal LLM can give accurate value estimates for search in software tasks.
answer_first_sentence: The effectiveness of our value function relies heavily on state-specific information and criteria, and providing the right context, such as file context, previous actions, and test outputs (Figure 1).
reviewer_status_quote: Although the authors explained some of those in their responses, I do not believe the paper can be improved in a short period of time.

concern: Discriminator debate unjustified; an accurate value function would make it unnecessary.
answer_first_sentence: The discriminator process step complements traditional MCTS approaches.

concern: Missing comparisons with MetaGPT, ChatDev, and GPT-Engineer agent frameworks.
answer_first_sentence: While we appreciate the reviewer's suggestions for additional comparisons, we note that tools like MetaGPT, ChatDev, and GPT-Engineer operate in fundamentally different settings from the SWE-bench benchmark [1,2].
reviewer_status_quote: Besides, the paper lacks of effecitve baselines, as is also pointed out by other reviewers.

concern: Rank metric is skewed by clusters of similar ENS variants; asks for one ENS variant.
answer_first_sentence: Evaluation metric – clustering of surrogates: we will include the comparison of one ENS variant with only RF and GP in the appendix of the revised version.
reviewer_status_quote: In the current light, the statistical test is still not meaningful to me since it still suffers from the problems I've outlined in the review.

concern: Mean-rank results hide absolute gains, which may be negligible late in optimization.
answer_first_sentence: Evaluation metric – absolute differences: we agree with the reviewer that the mean rank plot is relative, however this is why we provide a table of critical differences (see Appendix I, Table 6) to support the claim that ENS indeed outperforms other methods in a statistically significant way.
reviewer_status_quote: In the current light, the statistical test is still not meaningful to me since it still suffers from the problems I've outlined in the review.

concern: Ensemble weights from local accuracy on acquisition points are unmotivated and unablated.
answer_first_sentence: evaluating the accuracy of the competing models on the points generated through the optimisation of the acquisition function in the current iteration, rather than on an externally generated test set, allows us to assess the “local” accuracy of the models.
reviewer_status_quote: How do you define accurate? The mean prediction of a surrogate can only be accurate in specific areas of interest.

concern: Missing baseline choosing GP for continuous-only problems, RF otherwise.
answer_first_sentence: The baseline “GP if continuous only, RF otherwise” would however require computational efforts that would make it hard to include it in time for the revised version; we can discuss this in the paper.
reviewer_status_quote: You ran GP and RF individually. It is not required to run any additional experiments. Simply aggregate the results in a different way.

concern: Missing ablations: equal initial weights, oracle weights, and GP-plus-RF-only ensemble.
answer_first_sentence: Weight initialisation: we will include an ablation study with all equal initial weights in the revised version of the appendix.
reviewer_status_quote: Same also applies for the comparison against oracle weights.

concern: Compare against state-of-the-art results for each benchmark as a useful reference.
answer_first_sentence: Missing baselines: we will add a comparison of DensBO to the best surrogate per benchmark (virtual best surrogate) in the appendix in the revised version.

concern: Section 3.1.2 contradicts Section 1.3 on clean accuracy at K=1; explanation unconvincing.
answer_first_sentence: The difference between the two experimental setups is as follows.
reviewer_status_quote: A number of explanations for the two experimental setups are provided, but I think the organization and description in the main text would still be confusing to the reader.

concern: Optimization, targeted and black-box attacks untested; single path may fail targeted attacks.
answer_first_sentence: We will respond to W2/W3 together from three aspects below!
reviewer_status_quote: the defense that are effective against AA are not necessarily effective against L2-norm optimization-based attacks.

concern: Unclear whether attacks target the classifier only or the classifier plus purifier.
answer_first_sentence: We respond to this comment from three aspects.

concern: Typos, such as a wrong equation reference near line 264.
answer_first_sentence: We have revised the typos (see revised PDF).

concern: Allostasis not compared with homeostatic mechanisms or other neural adaptation frameworks.
answer_first_sentence: The allostatic aspect of the model is restricted to the fact that the numerosity acts as a variable set point to what would otherwise be a purely homeostatic mechanism.

concern: Only idealized controlled tasks; no test of robustness to noisy, unpredictable inputs.
answer_first_sentence: Thank you for your comment on this.

concern: Unclear neuroscience evidence for using a ring attractor bump to represent subitizing.
answer_first_sentence: The system for the number line we consider is linear for smaller numbers as portrayed in Leslie et al. (2008).

concern: Error analysis is thin; bump instability as a source of errors is not explained.
answer_first_sentence: The system uses a homeostasis system with the LGM and HGM perturbs the bump activity to move and this causes instability in the system to move the bump.

concern: Is bump instability driven by synaptic time constants or by network noise?
answer_first_sentence: The bump instability is caused by perturbations of spike made by the LGM and HGM.

concern: Asks for benchmarking against ring attractors with stabilizing feedback for drift.
answer_first_sentence: Thank you for your interest in this aspect of the model.

concern: Only Q-learning-based RL tested; modern deep RL such as PPO needed to show generality.
answer_first_sentence: The reviewer correctly points out that we only use Q-Learning-based RL methods in this work.
reviewer_status_quote: I still believe the experimental scope is not comprehensive enough to fully validate the framework's effectiveness across diverse RL paradigms and environments.

concern: Missing LLM-plus-RL baselines where the LLM directly generates actions and transitions.
answer_first_sentence: We appreciate the reviewer’s suggestions about including LLM + RL baselines, but we point out that the suggested baseline the reviewer discusses is essentially how the RLang-DynaQ-Plan agent works—in this case, RLang acts as an intermediary to convert action plans into a policy that can be run by the RL agent.

concern: Assumes human-written advice for every environment; asks whether LLMs could generate it.
answer_first_sentence: The topics the reviewer mentions have been the subject of existing works, but the focus of our work is precisely on how to ground human-given language in RL.

concern: Section 4.3 needs quantitative results such as grounding accuracy; a demo is not enough.
answer_first_sentence: We believe that the symbol-grounding via VLM demonstration in section 4.3 shows that VLMs can be used to obviate the need for some human annotations.
reviewer_status_quote: Moreover, the qualitative results in section 4.3 indeed can show an example of it, but it doesn't present metrics like its grounding accuracy, how integrating the system into RL can influence the final performance, etc. That's why the quantitative results are necessary.

concern: Asks why the DynaQ baseline fails in the Figure 6 experiment.
answer_first_sentence: This is a good question, similar to one that was raised by Reviewer 3iuj.

concern: Asks what the biggest challenges are for extending to high-dimensional continuous RL.
answer_first_sentence: This is an important question and we thank the reviewer for raising it.

concern: Stage-1 per-scene overfitting plus a network seems over-complicated; the network may be unnecessary.
answer_first_sentence: The utilization of a neural network at the first stage is indeed necessary, since the distributional randomness of vanilla-3DGS outputs cannot be fully regulated by the second stage.

concern: Claimed GS-space supervision advantage is weak; image supervision scores better on SSIM and LPIPS.
answer_first_sentence: First, we need to point out that both PSNR and SSIM metrics are the higher the better while the LPIPS metric is the lower the better.
reviewer_status_quote: I'm suspicious of the core argument that GS space supervision leads to better performance than image space supervision.

concern: Diffusion model design, with extra steps for alpha, scale, and quaternion, is confusing.
answer_first_sentence: During the training process, we find that jointly diffusing all 3D Gaussian attributes usually leads to collapse training (mainly because the dimension of the spherical harmonics is much more than other attributes).
reviewer_status_quote: The diffusion model described in this work is still very confusing. A better pipeline figure, formula, or algorithm table would be helpful in understanding.

concern: Stable diffusion back view and HaP point generator are existing works, not contributions.
answer_first_sentence: The stable diffusion model or the position generator alone cannot form our technical contribution.

concern: Is shape or texture the source of gains? Asks for texture remapped onto ground-truth shapes.
answer_first_sentence: It seems only feasible on GTA and SiTH by providing ground truth occupancy or SDF.

concern: Would front and back views alone, optimized into 3DGS, show texture mapping?
answer_first_sentence: Yes, we simply map the front and back view to the point cloud.

concern: Applications are niche; reviewer sees little significance beyond a narrow area.
answer_first_sentence: J-Orthogonality constraint problems defines an optimization framework that is fundamental to a wide range of models in statistical learning and data science, including hyperbolic structural probe problem[1;2], and ultrahyperbolic knowledge graph embedding [3].

concern: Theory and complexity against ADMM and UMCM not analyzed in detail, including baseline complexity.
answer_first_sentence: (1) ADMM only satisfies the KKT condition in Lemma 3.1 when t is sufficiently large（possibly-infinite）, whereas JOBCD satisfies the constraint for any iteration point.
reviewer_status_quote: Does that mean: the theoretical convergence is still the same for both ADMM and JOBCD, but you empirically found it's more effective after fine-tuning the parameter for ADMM?

concern: Stronger ADMM tailored to J-orthogonal constraints, or another SOTA method, is missing.
answer_first_sentence: We kindly refer the reviewer to the design process of the UMCM algorithm.

concern: Requests empirical convergence plots comparing BCD and ADMM across problem instances.
answer_first_sentence: For more experimental comparisons, we refer the reviewer to Section F.5 of the original manuscript.
reviewer_status_quote: Does that mean: the theoretical convergence is still the same for both ADMM and JOBCD, but you empirically found it's more effective after fine-tuning the parameter for ADMM?
